Will Smith welcomes third daughter before Dodgers NLCS Game 3
Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Will Smith became a father for the third time as his wife welcomed another daughter just hours before NLCS Game 3 against Milwaukee. While celebrating off-field news, Smith continues to work through postseason struggles at bat.
Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Will Smith welcomed his third child on Oct. 14, as his wife, Cara Smith, announced the birth of their daughter ahead of Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
Smith's third child is also his third daughter. Cara Smith shared the news on Instagram with a caption reading, “Our third October baby girl… Carter????.” Their first child, Charlotte Smith, was born in 2022 and their second daughter, Layton Smith, arrived in October 2024. The couple has had a new child every two years.
As he prepared for an important postseason game with the Dodgers trailing 0-2 in the series and needing more offense, Smith received this personal milestone off the field. Despite his recent struggles at bat—hitting just .043 with one hit in 23 plate appearances during the postseason—Smith said he remains focused on helping his team, “Yeah, I went back and looked,” Smith said. “I don’t know if it clipped it or whatever. It was kind of early in the game. We kind of had him on the ropes where we could just get him out there. And the walk, the walk one was a bummer but I guess it happens. It’s baseball.”
Smith missed some calls behind home plate during Game 2 that could have affected pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s outing by extending it through pitch challenges.
With another healthy baby girl now part of his family and extra motivation to perform well for both team and family, Smith will look to draw upon his experience as one of Los Angeles’ reliable players.
